notes.label: Modeled, not measured
notes.text: the per-order figures and the “$100 of sales” bars apply company-wide ratios from the filings to a hypothetical order. We found no order-level or per-bag cost data, and we don’t repeat the widely circulated but unsourced 40-lb-bag anecdotes.

notes.label: Not shown
notes.text: a daily IPET price series. The stock chart plots only individually documented closes, indexed to the IPO price.

notes.label: Secondary figure
notes.text: the ~$1.2M Super Bowl ad cost comes from secondary reporting, not a filing.

notes.label: Derived values
notes.text: Q2 ’99 marketing, the Nov 6, 2000 close, gross margins, ratios, runway quarters, marketing per net new customer, cap-table float and “others”, and the 270-day count are our arithmetic on sourced numbers.

notes.label: Not comparable
notes.text: rival funding figures mix single rounds and cumulative totals. Petstore.com’s fulfillment model wasn’t found in our sources.

notes.label: Map
notes.text: markers are placed at city level (Bay Area sites at street-address level, approximately). The exact address of the 2000 headquarters move isn’t confirmed. Distance rings are illustrative, not shipping zones.

notes.label: Archive
notes.text: several Wayback captures are missing images or substitute images from other dates. Captions flag each case.

notes.label: Reported, not confirmed
notes.text: PetSmart’s ~$3.35B price for Chewy (Recode/CNBC). Petopia’s ~60% layoff figure is from contemporary press.

notes.label: Gross margin scope
notes.text: Pets.com’s filings put fulfillment in marketing and sales, not in cost of sales. We found no filing that records a change in that classification, and none that gives Pets.com’s own fulfillment cost in dollars. The only fulfillment dollars in the record are Petstore.com’s, from Pets.com’s own pro forma reclassification.[^48]

notes.label: First-year rivals
notes.text: The four first-period columns cover different spans: they begin between Jan 28 and Mar 9, 1999 and end between Dec 31, 1999 and Jan 2, 2000. PetSmart.com had development months before its store launched on Jun 29, 1999.[^44] Petstore.com’s figures are in dollars and include fulfillment in cost of sales; the others are in thousands.[^48]

notes.label: Stock quotes
notes.text: The Nasdaq ranges come from the FY2000 10-K.[^6] The 2001 quotes are over-the-counter prices after the delisting. The FY2001 10-K says they are inter-dealer prices that may not represent actual transactions.[^40] The two venues are drawn separately and not joined.

notes.label: Current status
notes.text: The trademark statuses were read from USPTO TSDR on Oct 10, 2026, and the domain registration date from the .com registry on the same day.[^53][^54] The pets.com redirect is a Wayback capture of Dec 28, 2025.[^55] We could not connect to the live site, and TSDR cannot be searched by name or owner, so we checked only the five applications named. We found no source for who holds the sock puppet rights after 2002.

notes.label: Hakan entities
notes.text: The 2000 representation agreement names Brian P. Hakan & Associates, Inc.; the 2001 buyer of the puppet rights is Hakan Enterprises, Inc. The filings do not say whether they are the same company, so this page keeps them apart.

notes.label: Derived in the new text
notes.text: The phrase almost four years (Nov 21, 1994 to Oct 7, 1998), the phrase three days (Nov 4 to Nov 7, 2000) and the comparisons of Petstore.com’s fulfillment cost with its net sales and cost of sales are our arithmetic on sourced numbers.
